complete_expression_findings.old_source: Pustet AP258 / printed172 contains the entire catechumen invitation and entire petition through aggregentur, followed by the actual old cue Per Dominum and separately marked Amen. The spoken genuflection directions between the historical invitation and petition belong to that older ceremony and are not imported into the modern prayer body.
complete_expression_findings.whole_petition_relation: All invitation and petition words are independently old, after stress-accent, j/i, ligature, pointing and physical-wrap normalization. The source reads fecundas with its stress accent; no oe-to-e normalization is asserted. No substantive prayer word is inserted into either petition.
complete_expression_findings.optional_words: The old prayer has fixed nostris twice. Actual 1970 AP246 / printed253 marks nostris optional in both positions. The candidate preserves both parenthetical tokens, and study English preserves both corresponding parenthetical our tokens. This is an explicit 1970 choice fact, not a claim that Pustet printed optional words.
complete_expression_findings.ending: The old catechumen cue remains Per Dominum; it is never expanded into or equated with the new short ending. Actual 1970 AP246 locally prints the entire short formula and R. Amen after this exact petition. Therefore no general conclusion rule is required or inferred for this solemn intercession.
complete_expression_findings.formula_word_source: Pustet AP266 / printed180 prints the complete old short formula Per Christum Dominum nostrum and a separately labelled R. Amen. That different old context supplies only the formula words; the 1970 local catechumen prayer supplies applicability.
complete_expression_findings.roles_and_silence: The 1970 local rubric distinguishes the invitation, a silent prayer interval and the priest petition. Silence contributes no missing spoken words. The final Amen remains separately labelled R. No old kneeling directions, a modern rubric body, or a fabricated spoken bridge is added.
complete_expression_findings.secondary_control: Secondary digital 2002 AP193 agrees in the complete invitation, petition, optional-word facts and local short ending. The adjacent changed intercession III is not evidence for this IV or for unchanged later editions.

english_fidelity.finding: Complete and faithful project study translation of both old prayer texts and the independently old ending formula.
clauses: Our God and Lord preserves Deus et Dominus noster; ears of their hearts and gate of mercy preserve both objects of adaperiat.
Having received forgiveness of all sins through the washing of rebirth preserves the full remission/regeneration clause and its connection to being found in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Who always make your Church fruitful with new offspring preserves the fecundity image and nova semper prole.
Increase faith and understanding preserves both requested objects, and reborn in the baptismal font preserves the baptismal condition.
Gathered among your adopted children faithfully conveys adoptionis tuae filiis aggregentur.
Through Christ our Lord and separately marked R. Amen preserve the exact short conclusion and response without substituting a historical-human cue.
english_fidelity.authorship: New project study English only, not transferred Lasance/ICEL text.

finite_whole_expression_assessment.strongest_contrary_case: The complete modern execution is not printed as one uninterrupted 1862 unit with this short ending: the old ceremony has its own directions, fixed nostris and a different ending cue. A modern editorial arrangement cannot be cleared merely by observing that its individual words are old.
finite_whole_expression_assessment.assessment: This finite projection preserves two complete old petitions, explicitly reports two optional-word appointment facts, and selects an independently old conventional short conclusion by the exact local 1970 printing. It does not import modern creative additions or rearrange petition clauses. The modern contribution asserted here is a bounded execution relation, not a license or a claim that the old whole page already printed the modern ceremony. On that complete-unit assessment, source-local study publication is supported under the existing public-domain witness route.
